name: row_norm_rmsnorm
notes:
One parameterised program for every (rows, channels) of RMSNorm:
y[r, j] = x[r, j] * rsqrt(max(mean_j x[r,j]^2, eps)) * gamma[j], the detr
resnet's norm (8192 and 32768 rows of 16 channels, x5 and x4 per forward). x and
y are the chip's activation layout with one entity per ceil(channels/128) rows
(row r*chunks + c holds channels 128c..128c+127, lanes past channels zero), so
the kernel reads the rows the previous kernel wrote and leaves rows the next one
reads, with no repack and no host step between them. Dataflow per group of up to
128 rows: the squares reduce at one word per (row, chunk) (MULT.RC.VS + AGG.SUM
into the row's R_ACC lane, the next row's load riding in the same word), A =
rsqrt(max(squares/channels, eps)) is one straight-line word (the hardware rsqrt
of ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE, floored by ACC.MAX), then p = A_r * x and y = p * gamma at
one word per (row, chunk) each -- three words per (row, chunk) in all, the
datapath's floor for a norm whose result needs two multiplies after the
reduction. The full groups of 128 rows are one dynamic loop and a short last
group is emitted a second time with its own DS half, so a group's unused
bookkeeping lanes can never set a row's scale; the group's first row is built at
run time (LR6 += the group stride per group) because rows up to 32768 with
several chunks exceed a CR half. Every constant (1/channels, eps) is a scratch
row read through R0 -- in NX8 only CR0 and CR1 stay exact -- and the program
sets every LR it reads and loads its own mask row, so it runs after another
kernel as well as from reset (test_calls.py runs it twice back to back in one
XMEM, the second reading the first's y as its x). Limits: rows 1..32768 (the
host tiles rows only), channels 16..1280 (16 is the detr calls; the floor is the
NX8 block scale, not the program), eps > 0. Accuracy: the reduction, the rsqrt
and the two multiplies are exact in FP32 but the squares, A and p rows are 8-bit
row quantizations on the way through R_ACC, so the golden (fl

name: binary_div_row
notes:
One parameterised program for every (numel, inner <= 128): y[i] = a[i] / b[i mod inner]
with b broadcast as a row, inner a power of two so b's tiled rows (pack.py: row j lane l holds
b[(128j + l) mod inner]) repeat the values lane-aligned -- a's row r combines with b's one row,
no rotation. The shape reaches the program only through CRs and the row loop is dynamic, so a
whole call is one launch: 32768 elements is 256 iterations of the same two words. Dataflow: the
only way into R_ACC is a multiply result and the only route from R_ACC back into a multiply is a
store and a load, which in NX8 quantizes to the row's grid -- so 1/b cannot be carried at full
precision through a register, and the quotient is split once per call. r = the ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE
reciprocal of the tiled b row (resident in R1); u = 2 - b*r from an exact product and an exact
FP32 subtract seeded by a stored 2s row (a power of two, held exactly, in R_CYCLIC's second
slot); e = r*u - r, computed in the accumulator (ACC.SUB against an exact MULT.VE of resident
r by the CR constant 1.0) and stored tight -- e's row scale is max|r*(1-b*r)|, at most b*(one
step of r's row) ~ 6% of a lane's magnitude, so e's own store costs ~2^-8 of a lane instead of
the ~2^-5 a full-magnitude s = r*u row would. Because the split is exact Newton for the RESIDENT
r, r + e = (1/b)(1 - eps^2) with eps = b*r - 1 whatever r's own store did: r's quantization
costs nothing and the residual is eps^2. The row loop is then two words per a row -- word A
multiplies the a row resident in R_CYCLIC slot 0 by r and initialises R_ACC (ACC.ADD.FIRST),
word B multiplies the same a row by e (R0), accumulates (ACC.ADD) and stores the row
(ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE identity), also loading the next a row (rule 2) and carrying the branch --
and the last row is short and emitted straight-line with its own DS half, the row before it
straight-line too, so nothing loads past a's region. The measured distance over the
sweep is at most 2 steps of the output row'

name: binary_sub_col
notes:
One parameterised program for every (op, numel, inner) with broadcast = col:
y[r][j] = a[r][j] op b[r]. An entity is one row of a -- b holds `inner` values, one per row,
so a and y are [inner, numel / inner], one memory row per entity holding its numel / inner
features (lanes past that zero; ds() refuses a row longer than 128, and the whole quotient
refuses an inner that does not divide numel) -- the layout every activation on the chip uses,
so the kernel reads the previous kernel's rows and leaves rows the next one reads with no
repack; the host tiles only `numel`. Dataflow per row: two products (the only way into
R_ACC is MULT_RES) for add/sub/max -- word A multiplies the a row resident in R_CYCLIC slot
128 by the CR constant 1.0 and initialises the accumulator (.FIRST), word B broadcasts b[r]
(MULT.RC.VE of the resident ones row in slot 0, the scalar element 128 + r of Ra = R1
selected by LR5, read forwarded after its INC -- so `inner` is at most 128: b is resident
and the Ra index stays in range) and accumulates (ADD/SUB/MAX) and stores with
ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE identity; word A carries the load of the row the next word A multiplies,
so nothing waits. `mul` is one product: its row is one word (load next a row, multiply the
resident one by b[r], ACC.ADD.FIRST, store). The row loop runs inner - 1 times (the branch
reads LR1 before its same-word INC, so nothing ever loads row `inner`) and the last row is
emitted straight-line; every store names exactly its numel / inner live lanes in the DS, so
the lanes past them are written 0 for whatever reads y next. Every LR the program reads is
set by it and R_MASK is loaded from its own scratch row, so it runs after another kernel as
well as from reset. The ones row is a scratch fill (1.0), b is loaded once into R1. Limits:
op add|sub|mul|max, broadcast col, inner 1..128 dividing `numel` with numel / inner <= 128
(so numel is at most 16384); div and min and the other broadcasts are in `unsupported`,
each for a stated reason. Ac

name: unary_cos
notes:
One parameterised program for every numel: y = cos(x) elementwise, one 128-lane row
per iteration of a dynamic loop whose bound is a CR, so a whole call is one launch and the host
tiles nothing but numel (524288 elements is 4096 rows, 65552 cycles; a call takes 3*rows + 2 of
the 16384 addressable NX8 rows, so the declared numel maximum is 698880). x and y are the plain
activation layout, so the kernel reads the rows the previous kernel wrote and leaves the rows the
next one reads. The AaQ activates into memory only, so every multiplicand is an NX8 row: cos is
even, so the program works on the square -- s = x*x is one MULT.RC.VS of the cyclic window (the
square kills the sign, so no |x| pass; the pad lanes' zeros are harmless) and one identity store
-- and then the degree-8 Taylor polynomial runs as Horner over s with dyadic coefficients b8..b0
(7 significant bits, the MULT constant's width): p starts at b8 (MULT.EE off R0[0] = 1.0, the
ones row the prologue stores itself with exp2(0), so the host prepares no constant) and each
step p = p*s + bk is a MULT.RC.VV (s in cyclic slot 1, p in R1) plus one more MULT_RES (MULT.EE
off the ones row; b0 is CR1) and an identity store -- one NX8 round trip per degree, the four
intermediate p rows living in y's region. 16 words per row. The last row of a call is short and
is emitted straight-line with its own DS half (as is the row before it), so every store's scale
comes from the live lanes and lanes past numel are written 0; the intermediates of that row use
the same half, which is why the golden (reference.py) runs the same polynomial with the same
constants and models the kernel's every FP32 product/accumulate and NX8 round trip -- the
kernel's residual against it is one store's rounding, held at 2 steps. Every LR the program
reads is set by it, R_MASK is loaded from its own all-ones row and every accumulation is seeded
with a .FIRST form, so it runs after another kernel as well as from reset. Limits: numel
1..698880, input ra

name: binary_add_col
notes:
One parameterised program for every (op, numel, inner) with broadcast = col:
y[r][j] = a[r][j] op b[r]. An entity is one row of a -- b holds `inner` values, one per
row, so a and y are [inner, numel / inner], one memory row per entity holding its
numel / inner features (lanes past that zero; ds() refuses a row longer than 128, and
the whole quotient refuses an inner that does not divide numel) -- the layout every
activation on the chip uses, so the kernel reads the previous kernel's rows and leaves
rows the next one reads with no repack; the host tiles only `numel`. Dataflow per row:
two products (the only way into R_ACC is MULT_RES) for add/sub/max -- word A multiplies
the a row resident in R_CYCLIC slot 128 by the CR constant 1.0 and initialises the
accumulator (.FIRST), word B broadcasts b[r] (MULT.RC.VE of the resident ones row in
slot 0, the scalar element r % 128 of Ra = R0 selected by LR3, which doubles as the
run's lane counter) and accumulates (ADD/SUB/MAX) and stores with ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE
identity; word A carries the load of the row the next word A multiplies, so nothing
waits. `mul` is one product: its row is one word (load next a row, multiply the
resident one by b[r], ACC.ADD.FIRST, store). The rows of a are grouped in runs of 128
(the lanes of one b row): each run opens with a prologue word that loads its b row
into R0, the run loop branches on LR3 against LR10 (the run's trip bound) and the run
loop on LR4 against CRgf (mul's run loop branches on the old LR3, so its bounds are one lower:
CR7/CR10 vs CR11/CR8 for the other ops); the last row of the whole call is emitted straight-line, so
nothing ever loads row `inner`. Every store names exactly its numel / inner live lanes
in the DS, so the lanes past them are written 0 for whatever reads y next. Every LR
the program reads is set by it and R_MASK is loaded from its own scratch row, so it
runs after another kernel as well as from reset. The ones row is a scratch fill (1.0);
b is streamed from XMEM one

name: binary_add_none
notes:
One parameterised program for every (op, numel): y[i] = a[i] op b[i] for op in
add, sub, mul, max, nothing broadcast, so `inner` takes only 0. a, b and y are the chip's
activation layout with one entity (row i holds elements 128i .. 128i+127, lanes past numel
zero), so the kernel reads the rows the previous kernel wrote and leaves rows the next one
reads, with no repack and no host step between them. The shape reaches the program through
CRs only and the row loop is dynamic, so a whole call is one launch: 262144 elements is 2048
iterations of the same two words (4107 cycles) and the host tiles nothing. Dataflow per row:
the only way into R_ACC is a multiply result and a word has one MULT and one LOAD slot, so an
elementwise row is two words and both run the multiplier -- one word multiplies the b row
resident in R1 by the CR constant 1.0 and initialises R_ACC with it (ACC.ADD/SUB/MAX.FIRST),
the next multiplies the a row resident in R0 by 1.0, accumulates (ACC.ADD / ACC.ADD /
ACC.MAX) and stores the row with ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE identity; each word loads the row the *next*
one multiplies, so no word waits on a load and no separate counter or store word exists. `mul`
is one product per row instead of two (MULT.RC.VV of the cyclic a row against the resident b
row, ACC.ADD.FIRST and the store in one word) and its second word carries only the b load.
Two words per row is the floor for a two-operand elementwise op on a datapath with one LOAD and
one MULT slot per word: 15360 elements in 251 cycles, 262144 in 4107, both at 128 lanes busy in
every word that multiplies. The last row of a call is
short (numel - 128*(rows-1) lanes) and is emitted straight-line with its own DS half, as is the
row before it, which keeps the one-row-ahead prefetch inside the regions; a store's DS names
exactly the live lanes, so the row's scale never sees a lane past numel and those lanes are
written 0 for whatever reads y next. Every LR the program reads is set by it, R_ACC is
initialised by the .

name: unary_silu
notes:
One parameterised program for every (fn, numel): y = fn(x) elementwise, x and y
the plain activation layout (row r holds lanes 128r .. 128r+127, lanes past numel zero),
so the kernel reads the rows the previous kernel wrote and writes the rows the next one
reads, with no repack and no host step between them. Hardware-clean NX8: formats =
["dynamic"], every store an ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE (identity, exp2 or reciprocal), the
accumulators FP32, no ACTIVATE.EXACT and no BREAK. The three must-cover calls (silu at
30720, 98304 and 294912 elements, mobilevit_s cvnets_in1k) are three shapes of the same
program: the row loop's bound is a CR, so a call is one launch (2304 iterations of the
loop for the largest). Dataflow, the exp2_recip sigmoid: |x| by ACC.MAX of x*1.0 and its
negation, e = AaQ exp2 of -|x| log2 e (the argument is <= 0 in every lane because exp2 of
a positive input is an AaQ error; log2 e enters as the sum of two dyadic MULT constants,
one 8-bit constant alone would move the exponent by 4e-2 relative), q = AaQ reciprocal of
1 + e (the +1 is the ones row, which the program's own prologue stores with exp2(0), so
the host prepares no constant), w = e q (not 1 - q: a q row whose largest lane is 1.0 has
a 2^-7 step and e/(1+e) at |x| = 8 is 3e-4, so the difference would cancel; as a product
of the two rows it is quantized with a scale of its own), and the two signed branches are
joined by y = ACC.MAX of the products x q and x w -- for x >= 0 the larger is x q =
x sigmoid(x), for x < 0 both are negative and the smaller magnitude x w = x e/(1+e) wins,
which is why no compare and no sign test exists in the program. gelu_tanh is the same with
the sigmoid's argument 1.59576... (x + 0.044715 x^3), which is of x's sign, so only |a| is
built (one extra pass, t = t (1 + 0.044715 x^2) by ACC.ADD.FIRST of a MULT.RC.VV of the
row against itself held in Ra); relu, relu6 and neg are one word per row (the AaQ has relu
and relu6, neg is ACC.SUB.FIRST with an identity store). Cost: 11

name: layout_concat
notes:
One parameterised program for every (kind, numel): kind = concat puts y's leading
rows/2 rows from a's leading rows/2 rows and y's trailing rows/2 rows from b's leading rows/2
rows -- the channel-axis concat every MobileViT transformer block ends with, cat((x, out), dim=1)
-- and kind = copy is the slice copy, y's rows from a's rows with nothing read from b; a, b and y
are each numel elements, rows = numel/128 of the chip's activation layout (row i holds elements
128i .. 128i+127), so a producer that wrote a numel/2-element tensor left exactly the rows the
concat reads. Nothing interprets what is inside a row, so the kernel reads the rows the previous
kernel wrote and leaves rows the next one reads, with no repack and no host step. Dataflow per
row: the only way into R_ACC is a multiply result and a word has one LOAD, one MULT, one ACC and
one AAQ slot, so a copied row is exactly one word -- MULT.VE of the row resident in R0 by the CR
constant 1.0, ACC.ADD.FIRST, ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE identity to y row (LR1 at cycle start, added to the
pass's y offset) -- while the same word loads the row the *next* word multiplies (LOAD reads LRs
after the word's own writes, MULT reads R0 at cycle start) and steps the source pointer, the store
index and the branch counter, which is kept one ahead. That is one word per row, the floor for a
datapath with one load and one multiply per word: 20480 elements runs in 173 cycles, 196608 in
1549 and the declared corner of 698880 in 5473, with the multiply issuing in every word of both
loops (its lane occupancy is 100%; the MAC utilization the report prints is 0% because every
multiply is the identity by 1.0 -- a copy retires no MACs). The last row of each pass is peeled
straight-line without its prefetch, so no load ever names a row past a region, and a pass of no
rows (a copy's second) is skipped by its guard word, which is what lets one program serve both
kinds; the store's DS names all 128 lanes because numel is a multiple of 256 and every r

name: reduce_rows_mean
notes:
One parameterised program for every (kind, rows, n): y[r] = sum / mean / max of the n values
of row r of a (rows, n) matrix. x is the chip's activation layout (entity r holds its n values in
ceil(n / 128) consecutive rows, lanes past n zero), so the kernel reads what the previous kernel
wrote; y holds one value per entity, in lane 0 of its own row -- the shape a horizontal reduction
lands on, since AGG writes one R_ACC lane and ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE stores a row whose DS names one
active lane (its scale therefore comes from that lane alone, and the lanes past it are written 0
for whatever kernel reads y next). The row loop is dynamic (the shape reaches it through CRs only:
CR12 is the bound, CR15 the two DS halves, CR13 the store's single lane) and the row's chunk loop
is rendered per call, so a whole call is one launch and the host only tiles rows. Dataflow: one
word per x row -- MULT.RC.VE of the row resident in R_CYCLIC slot 0 by the exact CR constant 1.0
(sum, max) or MULT.RC.VV against the resident 1/n row (mean, which therefore reduces to the mean
directly with no quantized sum in front of it), AGG.SUM / AGG.MAX into R_ACC lane 0 seeded by the
.FIRST form at the row's first chunk, and at the row's last chunk the ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE identity
store; the next row's LD.MULT.CYCLIC rides in the same word (MULT reads R_CYCLIC at cycle start,
LOAD reads LRs after the word's LR writes), so the multiplier, the reduction stage and the load
unit are all busy every word: mobilevit_s's 640 x 64 mean is 645 cycles (2053 at
the 1024 x 256 pooling call, 99.8% MAC utilization), one word per row. The
LR sub-slots and the branch read cycle-start values, so the store's row is named by ADD LR2 LR4 CR0
from the entity counter before its INC and the branch tests the x row walk before its INC; two LR
sub-slots never write one register (fault F-3). The last entity of a call is emitted straight-line
with no load in its last word, which keeps the one-row-ahead prefetch inside x's region. Ever

name: conv2d_depthwise
notes:
y = conv2d(x, W) + bias for a depthwise window (groups == cin == cout), one
parameterised program for every (h, w, cin, cout, kh, kw, stride, padding, groups, bias):
the four mobilevit_s cvnets_in1k depthwise convolutions -- 128 channels at 128x128, 256 at
64x64, 384 at 32x32, 512 at 16x16, each 3x3 stride 2 same-padding with a bias -- are all in
the domain and each runs in ONE launch (cases.default/mv32/mv64/mv128 are those four at their
real shapes), the kernel walking each output pixel's window itself by row address (one row per
input pixel), so no im2col and no padded copy is ever built and no host step exists. x and y
are the chip's activation layout (pixel p holds its channels in rows p*ceil(cin/128)+c, lanes
past cin zero), so the kernel reads what the previous kernel wrote and leaves what the next one
reads, and the weights are prepared offline tap-major (row t*chunks+c is tap t's weight for
those 128 channels) so that one word multiplies a pixel's channel row by a tap's weight row
lane-wise: 128 channels of a window per multiply. Dataflow: the only way into R_ACC is a
multiply result and a word has one MULT and one LOAD slot, so a tap costs its two loads (input
row -> an R_CYCLIC slot, weight row -> R0) two words, each of which multiplies the previous tap,
and the word after the last load multiplies, accumulates and stores (MULT+ACC+ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE
ride one word): 19 words per output pixel per channel chunk at 3x3, 9 of them multiplying
(46% of the run's words, every multiplying word at all 128 lanes), which is what a window that
reads both of its operands from memory costs this datapath; 78095 cycles for the 128x128x128
call, 5037 for the 16x16x512 one. The output row loop and the interior-pixel loop are dynamic
(the shape reaches them through CRs and LRs only, so 4096 output pixels is 4096 trips of the
same words); the channel chunks (<= 4, so cin <= 512 by the 1024-word program) and the taps are
rendered. Out-of-image taps are not skipped -- a copy tha

name: binary_div_scalar
notes:
One parameterised program for every numel: y = a / b with b the one scalar of
its row (lane 0), broadcast over all rows. a and y are the chip's activation layout
with one entity (row i holds elements 128i..128i+127, lanes past numel zero), so the
kernel reads the rows the previous kernel wrote and leaves rows the next one reads;
b is one row whose lane 0 the host prepared offline. The shape reaches the program
only through CRs and the row loop is dynamic, so a whole call is one launch: 65536
elements is 512 iterations of the same two words. Dataflow: the only way into R_ACC
is a multiply result and the only route from R_ACC back into a multiply is a store
and a load, which in NX8 quantizes to the row's grid -- so 1/b cannot be carried at
full precision through a register, and the quotient is split once per call:
y = a*(r + e) with r the ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE reciprocal of the broadcast scalar (all
128 lanes of one row the same value, so its own quantization costs at most one step
of r) and e = (1 - b*r)*r the correction. b*r is an exact product, 1 - b*r an exact
FP32 subtract (b*r is within [0.5, 2] of 1, so Sterbenz makes it exact), the product
with the resident r is exact, and both factors are stored with the one-lane DS half
so they keep ~2^-7 of their own magnitude: the residual 1 - b*(r+e) is ~2^-13 of
1/b. The exact ones row the subtract is seeded from is built by ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE
exp2 of 0 (exp2(0) = 1, one distinct value, stored exactly) -- no packed constant
row, so nothing in the folder depends on the element format. Each row is then two
exact products a*r + a*e (MULT.RC.VE against R0[0] and R1[0], the cyclic a row
loaded one word ahead, rule 2) and one accumulator add, and the output row's own
quantization is the only error the golden sees -- measured max 1 step, tolerance
NX8_STEP/1. The last row is emitted straight-line, so no word loads a row past a's
region. Every LR the program reads is set by it, R_ACC is initialised by the
ACC.ADD.FIRST of every row a

name: binary_add_row
notes:
One parameterised program for every (op, inner, numel): y[i] = a[i] op b[i mod inner]
for op in add, sub, mul, max, b broadcast as a row (a bias). `inner` is restricted to multiples of
128 whose row count is a power of two (128..262144), so the repetition is lane-aligned (no
rotation) and b's row pointer LR2 wraps with INC.MODP2 (mod 2^k, k = log2(ceil(inner/128))).
a and y are the chip's activation layout (row i holds elements 128i..128i+127, lanes past numel
zero); b is ceil(inner/128) rows repeating, so a's row r combines with b's row r mod b_rows --
the t5/clip/whisper bias add, one launch per call (32768 elements = 256 rows = ~520 cycles).
Dataflow per row is binary_add_none's: two words, both running the multiplier -- word A multiplies
the b row resident in R1 by the CR constant 1.0 and initialises R_ACC (ACC.ADD/SUB/MAX.FIRST),
word B multiplies the a row resident in R0 by 1.0, accumulates and stores with ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE
identity; each word loads the row the next one multiplies. `mul` is one product per row
(MULT.RC.VV of the cyclic a row against the resident b row) and its second word carries only the
b load. The last row of a call is short and emitted straight-line with its own DS half, as is the
row before it, so the one-row-ahead prefetch stays inside the regions and the store's DS names
exactly the live lanes. Every LR the program reads is set by it and R_MASK is loaded from its own
scratch row, so it runs after another kernel as well as from reset. Limits: numel 1..262144,
inner in the power-of-two-row choices, broadcast row only (none/col/scalar and div/min in
`unsupported`, each for a stated reason); no FP32 variant. Accuracy: the products and the
accumulator adds are exact in FP32 and only the store rounds, so the golden (float64, quantized
row by row like the store) matches at max |err| 0, tolerance NX8_STEP 1 ulp.

name: binary_mul_scalar
notes:
One parameterised program for every (op, numel): y[i] = a[i] op b[0] for op in
add, sub, mul, max, broadcast = scalar (b is one value, `inner` 0). a and y are the chip's
activation layout (row i holds elements 128i .. 128i+127, lanes past numel zero), so the kernel
reads the rows the previous kernel wrote and leaves rows the next one reads, with no repack and no
host step between them; b is one row, the scalar in lane 0. The shape reaches the program through
CRs only and the row loop is dynamic, so a whole call is one launch: 45000000 elements is 351563
iterations of the same one-word loop (~351567 cycles) and the host tiles nothing but numel.
Dataflow: the scalar is loaded ONCE into R1 and selected by an LR src of 128 (R1[0]), so a row of
`mul` is ONE word -- it loads the next a row into R_CYCLIC (LD.MULT.CYCLIC, read by MULT at cycle
start, written after), multiplies the resident row by the scalar (MULT.RC.VE), initialises the
accumulator with the product (ACC.ADD.FIRST) and stores it (ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE identity): 128 lanes
busy in every loop word, 40960 elements in 325 cycles. add/sub/max need the scalar as a second
product and broadcast: word A multiplies the resident a row by the CR constant 1.0 (MULT.RC.VE
against CR1) and initialises the accumulator, word B broadcasts b (MULT.EE of R1[0] by 1.0),
accumulates it (ACC.ADD / ACC.SUB / ACC.MAX) and stores the row -- two words per row, the
multiplier busy in both. The last row of a call is short (numel - 128*(rows-1) lanes) and is
emitted straight-line with its own DS half; the loop's last load brings exactly that row into
R_CYCLIC, nothing ever loads row `rows`, and its store names exactly the live lanes so the row's
scale never sees a lane past numel and those lanes are written 0. Every LR the program reads is
set by it, R_ACC is initialised by the .FIRST accumulate of every row and R_MASK is loaded from
its own scratch row, so it runs after another kernel as well as from reset. Limits: numel
1..45000000, op add

name: gemm
notes:
One program for every (m, k, n, bias, act in none|relu): the shape reaches it through CRs and four
dynamic loops -- the output-channel tile loop (one R_ACC row is 128 channels), the token loop, the k
chunk loop and the input loop inside a chunk -- so a whole layer is one launch and the host only
tiles m. a is token-major (token i's k elements in rows i*chunks+c); w is *input-major*, row
t*ytiles+tt holding input channel t's weights for the channels tt*128..tt*128+127 (row k pads the
input loop's last prefetch; lanes past n are the packer's zeros); b is the n biases (row tt of its
ceil(n/128)-row region holds the biases of channels tt*128..tt*128+127, zero-padded past n -- so a
short last tile's store never sees a junk lane and its row scale matches the golden's); y is one
row per token and tile. The inner loop is the outer product: one word does MULT.RC.VE of the tile's
128 weights (R_CYCLIC slot 0) against the scalar a[i,t] (R0) and ACC.ADD into the tile's 128 FP32
accumulators, so each word is 128 useful MACs and the whole of k is contracted inside the kernel.
The word also prefetches the next input's w row (LOAD reads LRs forwarded) and steps the two
counters; the tile's b row sits in R1 for the whole pass, which lets the store word do the bias add
(MULT.VE x CR1 + ACC.ADD) and the ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE (identity or relu) in the same word. The input
loop's bound is the chunk's input count minus two (the branch reads the counter as the word began,
one behind the INC), the chunk loop's BNE reads the token's cumulative input count against
cfull*128, and LR3 (a's row) is reset at each tile pass -- the three details the loop bounds live
or die by. A short last chunk stops at k - 128*cfull inputs, and lanes past n of every w and b row
are zeros, so a short last tile's extra lanes multiply and store zeros under a full-row DS without
touching the row's scale. Every instruction is hardware (ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE stores, no emulator-only
op), every LR the program reads is set by i

name: row_norm_layernorm
notes:
One parameterised program for every (kind, rows, channels): layernorm
y[r] = (x[r] - mean_r) * A_r * gamma + beta and rmsnorm y[r] = x[r] * A_r * gamma, with
A_r = rsqrt(max(var_r, eps)) taken by the AaQ stage's hardware rsqrt (the approximation; the
variance is floored at eps by ACC.MAX first so the rsqrt never sees a negative). The shape
reaches the program through CRs and the row loop is dynamic, so a whole layer -- 1024 tokens x
144 channels -- is one launch; the host only launches (it may tile `rows`, the one dimension the
kernel does not loop over on its own, while `channels` is the kernel's own chunk loop, rendered
per call). x and y are the chip's activation layout (entity r owns ceil(channels/128) consecutive
rows, lanes past channels zero), so the output is the next kernel's input unchanged; gamma, beta,
the 1/channels and eps constant rows and the mask row are constants prepared offline. Dataflow,
per group of up to 128 rows whose bookkeeping lives one value per R_ACC lane: two reduction
passes at one word per (row, chunk) each (MULT.RC.VV of the row against the resident 1/channels
row then AGG.SUM, so the mean reduces directly with no quantized sum in front of it; then
MULT.RC.VS and AGG.SUM for the squares), the group's scalars straight-line (A = rsqrt of
squares/channels - mean^2 floored at eps, D = -(mean*A)), then p = A_r*x + D_r and y = p*gamma +
beta at two words per (row, chunk) -- a word holds one multiply-accumulate pair and y's three
products cannot meet in one of them, so the intermediate is stored once; rmsnorm needs neither D
nor beta and runs three words per (row, chunk). Every operand address is a CR base plus an LR
row, every LR is set before it is read, R_ACC is zeroed before each reduction and R_MASK is
loaded from its own row, so the program runs after another kernel as well as from reset (the
folder's test_calls.py runs the kernel twice back to back on one XMEM, the second reading the
first's y as its x). Limits: rows 1..1500 (128 per

name: unary_gelu
notes:
One parameterised program for every numel: y = gelu(x) elementwise, x and y the
plain activation layout (row r holds lanes 128r .. 128r+127, lanes past numel zero), so the
kernel reads the rows the previous kernel wrote and writes the rows the next one reads, with
no repack and no host step between them. Hardware-clean NX8: formats = ["dynamic"], every
store an ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE (identity, exp2 or reciprocal), no ACTIVATE.EXACT and no BREAK.
The must-cover call (gelu at 393216 elements, sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, x6 per
forward) is one launch: the row loop's bound is a CR, so 3072 iterations of the same words.
Dataflow: gelu is x * sigmoid(z) with z = c (x + 0.044715 x^3), c = 2 sqrt(2/pi) -- the tanh
form, kind estimation because its deviation from the erf form is at most ~3.4e-4 absolute
(around |x| ~ 2); the kernel's own constants hold the tanh form to 5e-6 relative. The sigmoid
goes through -|z| (exp2 of a positive input is an AaQ error): s = x^2 (one MULT.RC.VS),
m = -(log2 e) c - (log2 e) c 0.044715 s (two MULT.RC.VE and two MULT.EE of the ones row's
element 0 -- the row is the program's own exp2(0) store, the host prepares no constant;
each MULT constant is an 8-bit NX8 element, so each coefficient is the sum of two dyadic
parts), t = |x| (ACC.MAX of x*1.0 and its negation), e = ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE exp2 of the
MULT.RC.VV product t*m stored in the same word (the argument is <= 0 in every lane),
q = AaQ reciprocal of 1 + e stored into t's rows, w = e q (one MULT.RC.VV) stored into e's
rows, and the two signed branches joined by y = ACC.MAX of x q and x w -- for x >= 0 the
larger is x q, for x < 0 both are negative and the smaller magnitude x w = x sigmoid(z) wins,
so no compare and no sign test exists in the program. Two row registers serve all four
intermediates (s: x^2, m, e, w; t: |x|, q), so a call is 4*rows + 2 XMEM rows and 16 words
per row, 13 of them multiplying -- 393216 elements in 49182 cycles. The short last row of a
call is emitted strai

name: row_softmax
notes:
One program for every (rows, n): the row loop is dynamic and the row's 128-lane
chunks are rendered per call, so the shape reaches the program only through CRs and one launch takes a
whole call; the host only launches, and tiles `rows` when a call's two row-major regions would not fit
the 16384 addressable NX8 rows (2*rows*ceil(n/128) <= 16384, i.e. 4096 rows at n <= 256, which is the
declared maximum). Dataflow, the exp2 recipe -- max, exp2, sum, reciprocal -- four passes over the row,
one word per chunk where the single MULT slot allows: pass 1 aggregates x*1.0 into one R_ACC slot with
AGG.MAX (the first chunk seeds it, the rest take the running max) and ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE relu-stores it
into the row's scalar lane -- relu, not identity, because a row whose logits are all negative must shift
by 0 and not by a negative amount, which is what keeps the exp2 argument <= 0 (exp2 of a positive input
is an AaQ error); 2*max(x,0) >= log2(e)*max(x) in every lane, and the 0.56*max of slack swallows the
scalar row's own 2^-7 quantization. Pass 2 forms exp2(c1*x + c2*x - 2*max) chunk by chunk -- c = log2(e)
as two exactly representable dyadic terms, one MULT.RC.VE each, because an NX8 MULT constant holds at
most 7 significant bits and one of them alone would move the temperature, and every probability with it,
by 4e-2 relative -- and ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE exp2-stores the numerator row. Pass 3 reloads the numerator
chunks and AGG.SUMs them into R_ACC[0], then ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE reciprocal puts 1/sum in the scalar lane;
that value's own quantization, and the max's, are factors common to the row, so they cancel in the
output row's scale; the last chunk of each pass parks in R_CYCLIC slot 1, so a scalar's row is
never re-read after the scalar lands on it -- this is what keeps the round trip safe at every
chunk count, up to n = 2048.
Pass 4 multiplies each chunk by the scalar (MULT.RC.VE with the scalar named by LR0, read out of R0[0])
and ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE identity-stores y. There is no

name: unary_log
notes:
One parameterised program for every (fn = log, numel): y = log(x) elementwise, x and y
the plain activation layout (row r holds lanes 128r .. 128r+127, lanes past numel zero), so the
kernel reads the rows the previous kernel wrote and writes the rows the next one reads, with no
repack and no host step between them. Hardware-clean NX8: formats = ["dynamic"], every store an
ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE (identity, plus the prologue's own exp2(0) ones row), the accumulators FP32, no
ACTIVATE.EXACT and no BREAK. The two must-cover calls (log at 4096 and 65536 elements,
google-t5/t5-small) are two shapes of the same program: the row loop's bound comes from the CRs'
rows, so a call is one launch (512 iterations of the 14-word body for the larger). The multiplier's
only operands are the LOAD-filled stages, so the polynomial's serial dependences are NX8 row round
trips: the substitution u = x - 1.25 (dyadic: the scale is CR1's 1.0, the offset a MULT.EE off the
ones row in R1, which the prologue stores itself with exp2(0), so the host prepares no constant),
then u2 = MULT.RC.VS of the cyclic window and u3 = u2 * u (MULT.RC.VV against R0 = u), each stored
and reloaded once. The sum b0 + b1 u + b2 u2 + b3 u3 is pure FP32 registers: seeded with b0
(MULT.EE off the ones row) after the ladder has finished with R_ACC, then b3 u3, b2 u2 and b1 u
accumulate and the row is stored with identity -- 14 words per row. The b's are the dyadic roundings
of the degree-3 minimax monomials over the declared input range [0.5, 2] (truncation 8.5e-3, under
one output-grid step); reference.py computes the same polynomial with the same constants in float64
in the kernel's own accumulation order, so the kernel's residual is its four NX8 round-trips and
the FP32 adds, held to 6 steps of the output row's grid. The short last row of a call is emitted
straight-line with the DS half naming exactly its live lanes (and so is the last full row, which
keeps the one-row-ahead prefetch inside the regions), so lanes past n

name: pool2d_max
notes:
One parameterised program for every pool2d max call: y[oy,ox,c] =
max over the k x k window of x, padding dropped (a tap outside the image
contributes nothing to a max, which is exactly the padding the reference
computes). x and y are the chip's activation layout (pixel p holds its
channels in ceil(channels/128) consecutive rows, row p*chunks+c holding
channels 128c..128c+127, lanes past channels zero), so the kernel reads what
the previous kernel wrote and leaves what the next one reads, with no repack
and no host step. Dataflow: the only way into R_ACC is a multiply result, so
every tap is a MULT.RC.VE of R_CYCLIC slot 0 by the CR constant 1.0 and an
ACC.MAX; the first valid tap of each chunk walk takes ACC.MAX.FIRST (a flag
LR routes it), which clean-initialises R_ACC, so no -inf seed row is needed
and no register a previous kernel left can matter. The store is
ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE, preceded in its word by an idempotent MULT+ACC.MAX of the
last tap (AAQ reads the cycle's ACC result). The whole call is one dynamic
launch: a loop over the output pixels with the k x k tap grid inside it per
chunk (chunks unrolled, at most two), every bound a register (LR13 h, LR14 w,
LR15 k, CR11 out_w, CR12 out_h), so nothing is baked into the instruction
stream and one binary serves the whole domain; out-of-image taps fall
straight through to the pointer walk, and a skipped window row advances the
tap pointer by a whole spatial row, which keeps LR1 = (gy*w+gx)*chunks + c
exact. The resnet18.a1_in1k call (64 channels, 112x112, 3x3, stride 2,
padding 1) is 290039 cycles. Limits: kind max (avg is in `unsupported`),
channels 1..256, h,w 1..128, k 1..3, stride 1..4, padding 0..k-1 (the guard
is folded into y's shape: padding > k-1 leaves windows with no valid tap and
ACC.MAX.FIRST would seed from a stale register). Accuracy: the datapath is a
chain of exact FP32 maxima and only the store rounds, so the golden (float64,
quantized row by row like the store) matches at max |err| 0 on every c

name: unary_abs
notes:
One parameterised program for every numel: y[i] = |x[i]|. The datapath has no
absolute value, but the accumulator has MAX and a negate: per row, MULT.RC.VE multiplies the
x row resident in R_CYCLIC by the CR constant 1.0, ACC.SUB.FIRST puts -x in R_ACC, the same
multiply runs again and ACC.MAX takes max(-x, x) = |x| -- two words per row, both running the
multiplier, and no intermediate row, so the only rounding in the whole kernel is the output
store's ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE identity, which the golden applies to the same row (measured max
|err| 0, tolerance NX8_STEP 1 ulp). x and y are the chip's activation layout with one entity
(row i holds elements 128i .. 128i+127, lanes past numel zero), so the kernel reads the rows
the previous kernel wrote and leaves rows the next one reads; |0| = 0 keeps a zero-padded row
zero-padded. The shape reaches the program through CRs only and the row loop is dynamic, so a
whole call is one launch: 65536 elements is 512 iterations of the same two words (1027
cycles), the last row emitted straight-line with the DS half CR15.H so its scale comes from
the live lanes only. Every LR the program reads is set by it and R_MASK is loaded from its
own scratch row, so it runs after another kernel as well as from reset. Limits: numel
1..1048448 (8191 rows; the call takes 2*rows+1 of the 16384 addressable NX8 rows), fn = abs
(the general unary's other functions live in their own zoo kernels). There is no FP32
variant: FP32 addresses 4096 rows only and dynamic is the chip's NX8 type.

name: unary_exp
notes:
One parameterised program for every numel: y = exp(x) elementwise, x the
plain activation layout (row r holds lanes 128r..128r+127, lanes past numel zero) and y
written back the same way, so the kernel reads the previous kernel's rows and leaves rows
the next one reads. The shape reaches the program through CRs only and the row loop is
dynamic, so a whole call is one launch. Dataflow: the AaQ's exp2 rejects a positive
argument, so the exponent is shifted below the range's upper bound and the shift paid back
with exact dyadic MULT constants -- e = exp2((x - 8) log2 e) (x in two MULT.RC.VE terms and
-8 log2 e in two MULT.EE terms against the ones row, the program's own exp2(0) store, so a
constant term does not scale with x; the exp2 store rides the fourth word) and y = e *
exp(8) (two MULT.RC.VE terms, the identity store in the third word), 7 words per row. All
constants are exact dyadics an NX8 MULT constant holds; the only errors are log2 e's 7e-6
truncation on the argument (<= 1.1e-4 over x in [-8, 8], an 8e-5 relative error on y) and
the two 8-bit row round trips (e and the output store), measured ~1 NX8 step. The range's
upper bound is 2, not the 8 the -8 log2 e shift would allow, because the chip chains: the
next launch of this kernel reads this one's y = exp(x) as its x, and its exp2 argument
(y - 8) log2 e must stay <= 0, i.e. x <= ln 8 = 2.079; declared 2 (exp(2) = 7.39, a 7%
margin under 8), so a call at the range top leaves the chained call's argument at -0.89.
x below 8 would make the exp2 argument
positive (an AaQ error): declared [-8, 2]. Limits: numel 1..698880 (5460 rows; the call
takes 3*rows+2 of the 16384 addressable NX8 rows), fn exp only. Every LR the program reads
is set by it, every accumulation is seeded with a .FIRST form and R_MASK is loaded from
its own scratch row, so it runs after another kernel as well as from reset.

name: layout_copy
notes:
One parameterised program for every (kind, numel); kind = copy: y[i] = x[i] for
i in 0..numel-1. x and y are the chip's activation layout with one entity (row i holds
elements 128i..128i+127, lanes past numel zero), so the kernel reads the rows the previous
kernel wrote and leaves rows the next one reads, with no repack and no host step between them.
The shape reaches the program through CRs only and the row loop is dynamic, so a whole call is
one launch: 262144 elements is 2048 iterations of the same word (2049 words plus a 4-word
prologue). Dataflow: the only way into R_ACC is a multiply result, so each row is multiplied
by the CR constant 1.0 (MULT.VE of the row resident in R1, whose elements sit at Ra offset
128) and stored with ACTIVATE.QUANTIZE identity -- a copy at the store's own quantization,
which is the rounding the next kernel's input would see anyway. One word per row: the next
row's load rides in the same word (LOAD reads LRs after the same word's writes, MULT reads R1
as the word began), so the multiplier runs in every word of the loop and the loop's last
iteration loads the row the straight-line tail word stores. The last row is emitted
straight-line with its own DS half, so a short last row (numel - 128*(rows-1) lanes) stores
exactly its live lanes and writes lanes past numel 0 for whatever reads y next. Every LR the
program reads is set by it, R_ACC is initialised by the ACC.ADD.FIRST of every row and R_MASK
is loaded from its own scratch row, so it runs after another kernel as well as from reset (the
verifier runs it twice back to back, the second reading the first's y as its x). Limits:

chain has room for a second launch), kind copy only -- transpose (lane permutation across
rows) and concat (two input regions and a split the signature cannot carry) are in
